candidate.title: Bru-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina Bru-Seq schematic, a single route from bromouridine labeling of nascent cellular RNA through isolation/hydrolysis, anti-BrdU bead capture and elution to a broad cDNA library-preparation block. The graph preserves the depicted pre-capture hydrolysis. The supplied primary protocol instead fragments enriched RNA after elution; that implementation distinction is resolved explicitly in the Bru-Seq scope and correction records. BruChase-Seq is discussed in source papers but is not a target or alternative in this image. TruSeq is a library-preparation component. No unshown chase, sequencing or computational operations are added.

operations.label: Label with bromouridine
operations.description: During ongoing transcription in cells, bromouridine labeling marks newly synthesized RNA, producing a cellular RNA population containing the orange-starred nascent transcripts shown. The overview cartoon identifies the target and is not a separate preparative operation.
operations.mechanism: The primary protocol supplies bromouridine to living cells; the drawing labels the incorporated transcription substrate Br-UTP. The molecular conversion between these forms is not drawn or expanded.
operations.information_effect: Label incorporation links an affinity handle to RNA synthesized during the labeling interval. The subsequent selection therefore reports recently synthesized RNA rather than labeling every pre-existing transcript.

operations.label: Isolate and hydrolyze
operations.description: In the depicted route, isolate RNA from the cellular transcription context and hydrolyze it into short fragments before bead capture. The output remains a mixture containing both starred and unstarred RNA. The primary protocol places deliberate fragmentation after elution; this drawn operation is retained as a schematic transformation, not asserted as that protocol's execution order.
operations.mechanism: RNA isolation plus hydrolytic fragmentation are grouped under the source caption. The diagram does not identify the hydrolysis catalyst or RNA-end products.
operations.information_effect: Cellular/chromatin association is lost on extraction, and fragmenting RNA breaks intact-transcript continuity while retaining sequence and bromouridine on label-bearing fragments. Label specificity is established by the subsequent capture, not by isolation alone.

operations.label: Bead coated with anti BrdU antibody
operations.description: Contact the mixed RNA fragments with anti-BrdU-antibody-coated magnetic beads. Label-bearing RNA becomes bead-associated; the pale surrounding fragments do not continue along the captured-RNA route. This local input retains the pre-capture fragmentation history drawn in the schematic.
operations.mechanism: Affinity capture of bromouridine-containing RNA by anti-BrdU antibodies on magnetic beads. Beads and antibodies provide a selection support, not a second biological analyte or a catalyst that copies RNA.
operations.information_effect: The retained material is enriched for the bromouridine label. Its interpretation as nascent RNA comes from when the label was incorporated. The drawing provides no quantitative purity or capture-efficiency measurement, so enrichment is not treated as perfect biological specificity.

operations.label: Elute

operations.mechanism: Elution of Bru-RNA from the antibody-bearing beads; the primary source confirms the release without requiring its execution conditions in this architecture.

operations.label: Single strand library prep
operations.description: Convert the eluted enriched RNA into a cDNA sequencing library through the single broad block labeled Single strand library prep. The catalogue names reverse transcription, PCR and TruSeq preparation; these remain components of this one block. The primary workflow includes first- and second-strand cDNA synthesis, so the caption is not read as specifying the physical strandedness of the final DNA library.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription transfers the selected RNA sequences into cDNA, followed by preparation/amplification of a sequenceable DNA library. The primary protocol uses TruSeq reagents from end repair onward. Its RNA fragmentation occurs after elution; the separate hydrolysis already depicted in op_isolate is not silently moved or repeated in this graph.
operations.information_effect: The library carries sequence copies of the enriched recently synthesized RNA. The primary implementation supports strand-specific coverage across introns and exons and interpretation of mapped abundance as relative RNA synthesis during the label interval. A chase comparison is required for the source paper's RNA-stability application and is outside this depicted route. Sequencing and mapping explain the readout but are not additional drawn operations.

method_scopes.rationale: All five local operations belong to the Bru-Seq schematic identified by the card title, overview title and collection-page caption. The primary full text resolves its biological interpretation as cellular bromouridine pulse labeling, anti-BrdU enrichment and a strand-specific cDNA readout of nascent transcription. The supplied primary implementation performs RNA isolation, bead enrichment and elution before deliberate library-stage fragmentation (sections 2.2.3, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6.1). Accordingly, the graph's op_isolate -> s_fragments -> op_capture route preserves the drawing but is not claimed to reproduce the primary implementation's fragmentation order. The shared purpose and RNA-to-cDNA interface are supported, not identity of every preparation step. The paper's BruChase-Seq route and catalogue application papers do not expand this schematic's targets.
